title: Add a keyless cosign sign step to docker-publish.yml
description: In applications/mcp-gateway/repos/mongodb-mcp-server/.github/workflows/docker-publish.yml, job build-push: (a) add id-token: write next to contents: read under permissions; (b) add id: build to the 'Build and push image to dockerhub registry' step (docker/build-push-action) so its digest output can be used; (c) after the push, add sigstore/cosign-installer pinned by full commit SHA, then a step that runs cosign sign --yes on every pushed reference as ${DOCKERHUB_REPOSITORY}@${{ steps.build.outputs.digest }} (sign the digest, never a tag), using GitHub OIDC keyless signing (no COSIGN_PRIVATE_KEY secret). In both callers, docker.yml (job docker-push) and publish.yml (job docker-push, currently contents: read only), add id-token: write, because a reusable workflow cannot get more permissions than its caller grants. Constraints: keep every third-party action pinned by full SHA, as the existing steps are; add no new long-lived secrets; test on a prerelease release_channel run before merging to main. No deployment window or change freeze applies (none in sdlc/policy.json or the env files).
acceptanceCriteria: grep -n 'cosign sign' .github/workflows/docker-publish.yml returns a step that signs the image by @sha256 digest (steps.build.outputs.digest), not by tag
docker-publish.yml job build-push, and the docker-push jobs in docker.yml and publish.yml, each declare id-token: write, and sigstore/cosign-installer is pinned to a 40-character commit SHA

A prerelease run of docker.yml completes, and cosign verify <repo>@<digest> --certificate-identity-regexp '^https://github.com/OnFinance/mongodb-mcp-server/.github/workflows/docker-publish.yml@' --certificate-oidc-issuer https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com exits 0

verificationMethod.description: Re-run probe-cicd-env on mcp-gateway/mongodb-mcp-server at the merged commit. Expected: rule CICD-SIGN-01 no longer yields a result at .github/workflows/docker-publish.yml, and the observation for sebi-cscrf-2024:PR.IP.S2 records a signing step in the pipeline.

rootCause.description: The reusable docker-publish.yml was written with buildx provenance/SBOM only. No signing stage was ever added, and the docker-push jobs in the callers grant no id-token permission, so keyless signing could not run even if a step existed.
